content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices when the true outcome shows strong upward momentum or mean reversion to lower levels.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts overshoot after sharp price spikes and fail to correct quickly.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections following upward moves.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually adjusts.
- Fails to capture the true mean reversion speed; often lags behind actual price corrections by 2–3 days.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts; underestimates the impact of macroeconomic or policy-driven shocks.
- Underestimates the effect of seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns (e.g., summer vs. winter trends).
